references.text: Both verses describe that Jesus was not captured or taken because his hour had not yet come, which underscores God's sovereignty over the hour of suffering.
Here the motif is repeated that no one could seize Jesus, even though they wanted to, because his hour had not yet come.
After Jesus has spoken in the temple (as in 8:20), they try to seize him, but he escapes because his hour has not yet come.
Jesus confirms that the time for his death and exaltation has come, marking the end of the period when no one could seize him.
Here it is declared that Jesus' hour has come, ending the protection he had previously enjoyed in the temple.
Jesus voluntarily surrenders himself to captivity, showing that his hour has now come, in contrast to earlier attempts to seize him.
